title: High-resolution European soil property maps based on LUCAS and AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings
abstract: High-resolution soil property maps have a wide range of applications, e.g. policymaking and precision agriculture. Previously published maps covering the EU-27 plus the UK range in resolution from 250 to 30 metres depending on the soil property. In this work, we produced 10 m resolution maps for soil texture (clay, silt, sand), coarse fragments, pH and bulk density. They are the products of a machine-learning workflow trained on LUCAS soil datasets and using AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings as predictors. We performed hyperparameter tuning and training on Random Forests (RF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The best-performing models were ANN, with R 2 values ranging from 0.21 for coarse to 0.69 for pH. The best-performing ANN hyperparameters for each soil property were used to produce soil property maps over Europe as well as uncertainty estimate maps obtained from Monte Carlo dropout. The generated maps aim to close the resolution gap for the EU-27 + UK and provide a promising baseline for precision agriculture, soil health assessment at field scale and spatial planning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Dataset for Visual Detection of Litchi Fruit Borer Infestation and Anthracnose
abstract: The litchi industry has long been severely plagued by the litchi fruit borer ( Conopomorpha sinensis ) and litchi anthracnose ( Colletotrichum gloeosporioides ). Despite the rapid development of deep learning in agricultural monitoring, there is currently no public dataset that supports the simultaneous detection of these two stresses, let alone a systematic simulation of variable lighting conditions in real postharvest environments. To address this issue, we constructed LitchiPestDisease—the first multi-illumination image dataset dedicated to the detection of litchi fruit borer infestation and litchi anthracnose. This dataset contains images collected from the core production areas in Maoming, Guangdong, China, during 2024 and 2025. To support the simulation of realistic grading scenarios, the dataset includes the original images and three systematically enhanced illumination variants (front lighting, back lighting, and side lighting) generated following the protocol described in this paper. All these images are provided in the public repository. The pest subset includes 3,061 original images, all annotated with bounding boxes for borer damage holes. The disease subset consists of 3,644 original images, a portion of which are additionally annotated with polygon instance segmentation, where each lesion is labeled by its severity (mild, moderate, severe). The corresponding enhanced images under three lighting conditions are fully provided in the public repository. Benchmark experiments based on YOLOv12n validated the effectiveness of the dataset: severe anthracnose detection reached near-perfect mAP50 levels, while pest detection achieved an mAP50 of 0.6539 under mixed lighting conditions. Comparative analyses across different lighting conditions and disease severity levels revealed the robustness and limitations of the model (e.g., the recall rate for mild disease under side lighting dropped to 0.878). Furthermore, benchmark experiments on instance segmentation revealed the performance variation of segmentation models under different lighting conditions, jointly providing a multi-task evaluation benchmark for algorithm optimization. LitchiPestDisease provides an important benchmark resource for the intelligent detection of fruit quality in real-world scenarios.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Comprehensive Multimodal Gait Dataset for Lower-Limb Wearable Robotics in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
abstract: Daily walking locomotion exhibits variability, asymmetry and ground constraints. Recording and analyzing real-world locomotion data is essential for expanding the application scenarios of wearable robots such as exoskeletons and prostheses. However, most existing gait datasets are collected with specialized equipment under predefined laboratory conditions, lacking visual information from natural walking environments and annotations for transitional states across different surfaces. To address this problem, we collected walking data from 17 healthy participants across diverse indoor and outdoor environments, including kinematic data from seven inertial measurement units (IMUs), foot pressure data from force sensing resistors (FSRs) with 96 points, and visual data from three front-facing cameras with 1280 × 720 resolution. All modalities are time-synchronized, with 448 clips and 243607 data frames in total. Full annotations are provided, covering 16 classes of lower-limb locomotion states (8 steady states, 8 transitional states), bilateral gait phases and bilateral coordinates of the center of pressure (COP). This dataset can be utilized for exploring the applications of machine learning in locomotion state recognition and intelligent control of lower-limb wearable robotics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Labelled Dataset of Healthy and Diseased Maize from Tanzania
abstract: Early detection of crop diseases is essential for improving maize productivity and strengthening food security, particularly in regions where agriculture is the main source of livelihood. This paper presents a labelled image dataset of healthy and diseased maize leaves collected in Tanzania to support the development of machine learning models for crop disease diagnosis. The dataset includes data on: healthy leaves, and diseased leaves of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) and Maize Streak Virus (MSV) which are among the most significant threats to maize production in the country. All images are annotated to support tasks such as image classification, object detection and image segmentation. The dataset comprises a total of 243,539 labelled images covering multi-season, making it one of the largest publicly available maize image datasets from Tanzania. It serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners advancing artificial intelligence applications in agriculture.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A spatially and temporally aligned contrast-non-contrast cardiac CT dataset of pigs
abstract: Traditionally, cardiac CT imaging relies on the use of contrast agents. However, in some cases such agents cannot be used, and there is a need to develop novel AI-based algorithms to accurately segment cardiac structures from CT images, recorded without the use of contrast agents. To address this challenging problem, we have collected a spatially and temporally aligned cardiac CT dataset of pigs with and without the use of contrast fluid. This dataset consists of 10 different pigs, CT-scanned multiple times between 15 and 130 kg to cover a wide set of body weights. A subset of the dataset is manually labelled, to enable development of supervised learning-based segmentation techniques.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Grid2Text Dataset Aligning Meteorological Grid Data with Expert Reasoning Chains
abstract: Accurate meteorological forecasting is fundamental to public safety and economic stability, but it heavily relies on numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, whose complex outputs are often inaccessible to non-experts. Although large language models (LLMs) show potential in translating structured data into natural language to automate forecast reporting, progress has been constrained by a critical scarcity of datasets that bridge the modality gap and capture the implicit reasoning of human experts. To address this, we present Grid2Text , a rigorously developed dataset aligning ERA5 meteorological grid features with expert-verified textual forecasts, encompassing explicit reasoning chains for temperature trends, wind vector transitions, humidity ranges, and precipitation types. Furthermore, we establish validation benchmarks derived from a human-in-the-loop workflow to ensure the physical consistency and logical accuracy of the data. We anticipate that this open-access dataset will catalyze the development of interpretable LLM approaches for weather forecast discussions, ultimately advancing the field of scientific text generation.

title: Refined annotations of intrahepatic portal and hepatic veins from thin-slice CT images
abstract: Accurate segmentation of intrahepatic vessels in contrast-enhanced CT is limited by spatial resolution, variable contrast timing, and the complexity of peripheral vascular anatomy. Public datasets such as the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08 include annotations of hepatic structures but provide incomplete delineation of small-caliber portal and hepatic veins. This work describes HVA-CT (Hepatic Venous Annotations CT), a dataset derived from the contrast-enhanced thin-slice CT volumes of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08, in which intrahepatic venous structures were re-annotated with more complete anatomical delineation. The dataset comprises refined three-dimensional segmentations of portal and hepatic venous systems generated through a structured workflow combining baseline model outputs, AI-assisted vessel branch identification, and expert review. For each case, updated venous segmentation masks, liver segmentations, and a standardized tool for intrahepatic vessel extraction are provided. The dataset is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated methods for hepatic vessel segmentation and analysis.

title: A Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset
abstract: In the field of motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCI), researchers have developed multimodal BCI systems that leverage the complementary spatiotemporal characteristics of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). This integration has been shown to substantially improve the accuracy and robustness of decoding movement intentions. However, publicly available synchronous EEG-fNIRS datasets for motor imagery tasks remain scarce. Such scarcity severely constrains the development of multimodal fusion algorithms. To address this gap, we introduce and openly release the Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset (SEFMEID), a concurrent hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset collected from 50 healthy participants. The dataset includes resting baseline, left-right hand motor execution (ME), and left-right hand motor imagery (MI) conditions, with each subject performing 25 trials for the right task and 25 trials for the left task. We also provide single-modality and multimodal classification results, as well as neurovascular coupling analyses, to validate the usability and quality of the dataset. In the deep learning results, the multimodal fusion algorithm achieves an improvement of approximately 10% over the best-performing unimodal approach. The public release of SEFMEID aims to serve as a valuable resource for advancing multimodal MI-BCI algorithms, investigating neurovascular coupling mechanisms underlying motor imagery, and accelerating clinical translation in neurological rehabilitation.

title: An observation-based daily gridded precipitation dataset for forecast verification
abstract: As numerous artificial intelligence (AI)-based weather forecasting models are trained by climate reanalysis, there is an urgent need for independent observation-based datasets for forecast verification. Mainly based on the Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN), this paper develops the GHCN daily gridded precipitation (GHCNdgp) dataset, covering the period from 2020 to 2025. Specifically, two daily station-based observation datasets–GHCN daily and Global Surface Summary of the Day–and three subdaily datasets–GHCN hourly, Integrated Surface Database and Integrated Global Land surface Dataset–are integrated to enhance global station density and spatial coverage. The spatiotemporal consistency checks are combined with integrity and reporting time checks to identify anomalous observations and infer stations’ reporting times. Furthermore, the GHCNdgp is compared against three existing precipitation products using Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), i.e., the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) V07 Late, the Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation (MSWEP) V2.8 and the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre (GPCC) First Guess Daily product. The results show that more than 90% of the anomalous observations come from identical values and duplicate sequences. The median PCC for stations with daily accumulation periods shifted by 24 hours is generally below 0.25. The quality control checks improve the median PCC from 0.46 to 0.62 under the IMERG, from 0.54 to 0.71 under the MSWEP and from 0.33 to 0.47 under the GPCC. These findings indicate that the GHCNdgp dataset effectively mitigates mismatches in observation reporting times and aligns with the grid resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° common in AI weather forecasts. This dataset is publicly available on Zenodo in the Network Common Data Form format, providing essential ground-truth precipitation observations specifically for benchmarking AI weather forecasts.

title: Beyond built-up land: Mapping complete settlement footprint in China from 1990 to 2020 with Landsat imagery
abstract: Accurate mapping of human settlements is vital for understanding urbanization, human-environment interactions, and sustainable development. Existing medium-resolution products often underestimate the real spatial extent of settlements by focusing solely on built-up cores. Here, we present the China Settlement Footprint 1990–2020 (CSF30) dataset, a nationwide product depicting complete human settlement footprints from Landsat imagery at five-year intervals. CSF30 was generated using an Entity-Based Image Analysis framework integrated with a deep learning architecture. To ensure spatio-temporal generalizability and boundary accuracy, the model was trained via a two-stage strategy utilizing a built-up area dataset and a newly annotated settlement footprint dataset. Comprehensive validation demonstrates that CSF30 achieves a mean F1-score of 0.91 across the 30-year period, showing distinct advantages in representing rural and peri-urban areas compared to existing products. CSF30 provides a critical, high-quality baseline for diverse applications, including investigating settlement trajectories, assessing ecological and environmental impacts, and monitoring progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: High-resolution dataset of core needle prostate biopsies with expert pathologist annotations
abstract: We present an expert-labelled image dataset designed to support automated analysis of image-guided prostate core needle biopsies (CNBs) in the context of prostate cancer diagnosis. The dataset includes 37 whole slide images (WSIs), corresponding to 60 CNBs stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), from 32 patients. The dataset contains 15480 manual expert annotations, covering benign glands, tumor, stromal tissue, adipose tissue, nerves, nerve ganglia, blood vessels, muscle, and inflammatory cells. Additional recorded features include stromal retractions, normal and abnormal glandular secretions, and tissue or digital image artifacts. These annotations represent the normal findings that pathologists encounter in routine diagnosis. The annotations were performed by two experienced uropathologists with final labels determined by consensus; immunohistochemical techniques were used as guidance. This dataset provides a foundation for training and benchmarking machine learning models for prostate biopsy assessment and is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Vineyard RGB-D, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK datasets for grapevine segmentation and localisation to enable autonomous robotic pruning
abstract: Agricultural robotics is becoming increasingly relevant for executing arduous tasks where human labour is scarce. Grapevine pruning is a seasonal task that, when performed manually, requires a worker to perform selective cutting of the grapevine canes. For a robot to conduct this type of task autonomously, it needs to navigate the vineyard rows without colliding with the grapevines, as well as retain information regarding each grapevine to perform the operation. This work presents datasets collected in a vineyard, comprising RGB and depth images, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK data, acquired using both a handheld device and a mobile robot. Furthermore, 494 RGB images obtained from the handheld device recordings were annotated with segmentation masks in YOLO format. The datasets support the development and evaluation of computer vision, localisation, mapping and sensor fusion algorithms for autonomous robots. Technical validation demonstrates the consistency and usability of the annotated data for training deep learning models.

title: A high-resolution global flood susceptibility dataset derived from multi-source earth observation and geospatial data
abstract: Floods are among the most damaging disasters worldwide, necessitating high-resolution modeling of where terrain and environmental conditions predispose societies to flooding. While geospatial data are invaluable for flood susceptibility mapping, comprehensive and globally consistent datasets remain scarce. We present the Global Flood Susceptibility Map (GFSM v1), a globally harmonized 30 m flood susceptibility dataset produced by incorporating multi-source flood conditioning factors accounting for topographic, hydrological, meteorological, and anthropogenic characteristics within a machine learning framework. A gradient-boosted tree model was trained on ~17,000 curated grid tiles with ~30.45 million training samples, using a global flood inundation dataset as training labels and nine conditioning factors (elevation, slope, aspect, wetness index, vegetation index, height above nearest drainage, water/roads proximity, and rainfall frequency). The model was deployed based on geopolitical and climate strata (units n = 192) to generate global pixel-level susceptibility. Rigorous cross-validation indicates strong model predictive accuracy (median area-under-curve ~0.95), and the output captures localized flood-prone regions worldwide. GFSM v1 offers a global open-source, high-resolution resource to support informed flood risk management, particularly in data-sparse regions.

title: CTX-UXO: Contextual visual dataset for localisation, classification and identification of unexploded ordnance
abstract: Unexploded Ordnances (UXOs) are explosive weapons that failed to detonate during deployment, posing significant threats to civilian safety and post-conflict recovery. The Contextual Vision for Unexploded Ordnances (CTX-UXO) dataset addresses this challenge by providing 3520 high-resolution RGB images, median size 2124 px square, containing UXOs collected over four years across all seasons and weather conditions. The dataset encompasses 15 449 annotated instances labeled as UXOs, with twelve subcategories for identification tasks, in which mortar bombs, projectiles and grenades constitute the predominant classes, supporting systems research and development in UXO classification, detection, instance segmentation and related applications, and providing multiple labelling formats such as YOLO and COCO. For the detection task including binary classification, an end-to-end solution for training, validation and testing is available as a reference by presenting a neural network optimized for edge deployment, Faster-RCNN with MobileNet V3 backbone, deployed for real-time inference with reduced costs on Nvidia Jetson Orin, achieving up to 23 frames per second with 62.18% Ap50 for UXO localisation and binary classification.

title: Long-term seasonal ruminant livestock distribution datasets in China’s grazing production systems
abstract: Accurate spatial distribution data of grazing livestock are essential for rangeland management and sustainability assessments, yet existing global datasets lack production system differentiation and seasonal resolution. We present China’s Long-term Ruminant Livestock Distribution in Grazing Livestock Production Systems (CLRD-GLPS) dataset, providing seasonally resolved distributions of cattle, sheep, and goats across China’s grazing systems from 2000 to 2021. The dataset was generated using a stacking ensemble machine learning framework integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, combined with interpretable machine learning for livestock segmentation. CLRD-GLPS includes 1-km resolution gridded maps distinguishing warm-season and cold-season distributions, with CV-based model-uncertainty layers. Model validation on independent test data achieved R 2 values of 0.954–0.961 for cattle and 0.896–0.915 for sheep/goats. External validation at city level yielded R 2 of 0.74–0.81, supporting dataset reliability across spatial scales. The dataset addresses critical gaps in livestock distribution mapping by separating grazing from non-grazing systems and capturing seasonal dynamics, supporting applications in forage-livestock balance assessment, climate impact studies, and evidence-based policy development.

title: A Pan-European Multimodal Dataset Linking Field Photos with Satellite Image Time Series for Agricultural Mapping
abstract: AgroFusion is a continental-scale, multimodal, pixel-based reference dataset designed to support rigorous evaluation and reproducible research in agricultural remote sensing and geospatial Artificial Intelligence (AI). Built upon the 2018 and 2022 Land Use/Cover Area frame statistical Survey (LUCAS), the dataset integrates 211,483 field observations (107,642 in 2018 and 103,841 in 2022), each linked to field photos (four cardinal views, point centered view, and a close-up), LUCAS land-cover and land-use annotations, with monthly pixel-based Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8, agrometeorological data from ERA5-Land, topography from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, soil properties from AI4SoilHealth, and annual embeddings from AlphaEarth geo-foundation model. AgroFusion is the first continental-scale resource for pairing geo-tagged field photos with pixel-based SITS, semantically rich agricultural covariates, and precomputed foundation model embeddings. This combination will enable a wide range of applications, including multimodal and multiscale crop type classification and phenology retrieval, and the interpretation of satellite-derived agricultural products using ground-level visual context.

title: A curated comprehensive dataset of asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction
abstract: The asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction is one of the key methods for constructing chiral β-aminocarbonyl moieties that occur in the structures of many biologically active compounds, including drugs. The selection of a catalyst and reaction conditions that ensure high enantioselectivity for specific substrates remains a largely empirical task. The scarcity of structured, openly available data hinders the application of machine-learning methods to enantioselectivity prediction and rational catalyst design. We present a dataset of 4015 reactions manually extracted from 153 publications spanning 2000–2025 and covering 468 unique organocatalysts. The structures of the reagents and catalysts, the reaction conditions, and the target values ( ee , ΔΔG‡) are provided in a machine-readable form suitable for training AI-models.

title: Renewable generation and electricity consumption datasets for energy market models generated with artificial intelligence
abstract: Analysis of future energy scenarios requires comprehensive and reliable input datasets. Open-access datasets increase transparency and reduce barriers to entry in modeling. In our study, we use artificial neural network models to transform 43 years of weather reanalysis data into hourly resolution, nationwide time series of renewable energy production (solar, onshore and offshore wind) and electricity consumption datasets. During our research, we developed a data quality control procedure for the ENTSO-E hourly-resolution database based on heat maps, histograms, and z-score values, thereby ensuring that our artificial intelligence models learn from high-quality data. Modeling was performed for all European countries with sufficient data quantity and quality to train machine learning models. The proposed neural-network-based database combines the widest spatial coverage among the reviewed datasets with accuracy that in most cases exceeds existing solar, wind, and electricity consumption databases, making it a valuable complement for European electricity system modelling. The open-access data series created can be used directly as input data for electricity market models, e.g., in unit commitment, network load distribution and pricing studies, and are also particularly suitable for analyzing the frequency, duration, and regional overlap of periods of low renewable energy production (Dunkelflaute events).

title: PRIME-CVD: Paired Synthetic Cohort and Structured EMR-Style Data Assets for Education in Cardiovascular Risk Modelling
abstract: In recent years, progress in medical informatics and machine learning has been accelerated by the availability of openly accessible benchmark datasets. However, patient-level electronic medical record (EMR) data are rarely available for teaching or methodological development due to privacy, governance, and re-identification risks. This has limited opportunities for students from healthcare and clinical backgrounds to gain hands-on experience in coding, data management, and cardiovascular risk modelling. Here we introduce PRIME-CVD, a parametrically rendered informatics medical environment designed explicitly for medical education. PRIME-CVD comprises two openly accessible synthetic data assets, each representing 50,000 adults undergoing primary prevention for cardiovascular disease and parameterised to reproduce the statistical characteristics of a derivation cohort from the Australian New South Wales Lumos linked-data resource. The datasets are generated entirely from a user-specified causal directed acyclic graph parameterised using characteristics of the reference cohort, publicly available Australian population statistics and published epidemiologic effect estimates, rather than from patient-level EMR data or trained generative models. Data Asset 1 provides a clean, analysis-ready cohort suitable for teaching exploratory analysis, stratification, statistical coding, and survival modelling, while Data Asset 2 systematically transforms the same cohort into a structured relational, EMR-style database with deliberately introduced data-quality challenges, including missingness, heterogeneous terminology, inconsistent measurement units, and cross-table linkage requirements. Together, these complementary assets enable healthcare and clinical learners to develop practical skills in coding, data cleaning, harmonisation, cohort reconstruction, and cardiovascular risk modelling without exposing sensitive information. Because all individuals and events are generated de novo, PRIME-CVD preserves realistic subgroup imbalance and risk gradients while ensuring negligible disclosure risk. Although the released PRIME-CVD cohort represents adults with no prior history of cardiovascular disease undergoing primary-prevention risk assessment, the complete data-assembly pipeline is provided through the dedicated GitHub repository. Educators may adapt the supplied code, parameters, and data-generating assumptions to construct alternative synthetic cohorts suited to their own teaching objectives. PRIME-CVD is released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence to support reproducible and scalable health data science education.

title: Nationwide annual agricultural land-use maps of Germany from 1990 to 2023 derived from satellite imagery
abstract: We present German-wide annual agricultural land-use maps from 1990 to 2023, created from Landsat and Sentinel-2 images using a deep learning approach. Based on farmers’ declarations from 2006 to 2022, we extracted annual training samples for 13 crop classes and one grassland class. These samples were used to train a multi-year one-dimensional convolutional neural network, which was subsequently applied to generate the annual land-use maps. Between 2010 and 2022, overall map accuracies ranged between 85% and 93%. When averaged over time, dominant classes like grassland, rapeseed, winter cereals, sugar beet, and maize were detected with high accuracy (≥90%). Conversely, minor classes such as fallow land and plantation were predicted with low accuracy (≤52%). Comparison of map areas with agricultural statistics over time revealed high correlations for most classes, particularly maize ( r = 0.978). The presented maps provide an essential basis for analyzing long-term trends in agricultural land-use. They can be used to fill temporal gaps in national agricultural statistics and to disaggregate those statistics to higher spatial units.

title: A Multi-Center, Multi-Modal Chest CT and Clinical Dataset for Differentiating Pulmonary Aspergillus from Non-Aspergillus and Non-Fungal Infections
abstract: Pulmonary Aspergillus infection (PAI) presents a critical diagnostic challenge due to its clinical management differing significantly from that of pulmonary non- Aspergillus fungal infection (PNAFI) and pulmonary non-fungal infection (PNFI). While Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution for rapid triage, its development is currently severely bottlenecked by data scarcity. Existing studies primarily rely on small, private, and single-center datasets, which hampers the generalizability of models and precludes reproducible research. To date, there is no publicly available, multi-center benchmark dataset that integrates imaging with key host immune factors for this domain. To address this critical gap, we present the first comprehensive, open-access dataset of its kind, collected from 569 patients across 4 hospitals in China. This dataset comprises: (1) standardized volumetric chest CT scans in NIfTI format; (2) a curated clinical record containing definitive diagnostic labels, demographics, and critical laboratory variables (e.g., lymphocyte counts, D-dimer). Technical validation was conducted for two binary tasks: Task 1, Fungi vs Non-Fungi, and Task 2, Aspergillus vs non- Aspergillus . This study introduced three models for classification: a clinical model using clinical variables, an imaging model based on CT images, and a fusion model combining both clinical variables and CT images. Model performance was evaluated through receiver operating characteristic analysis, with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) reported as key metrics. As a rare and versatile resource, this dataset supports not only the development of robust AI classification algorithms but also facilitates clinical prediction modeling, the investigation of the predictive role of host variables (e.g., age, comorbidities), decision-making regarding invasive interventions, and radiological education, thereby accelerating precision medicine in pulmonary infectious diseases.

title: A paediatric dataset of non-dermoscopic skin images for dermatological AI research
abstract: This paper introduces DermoPed, a non-dermoscopic dermatology dataset composed almost entirely of paediatric patients’ images. The long-term goal is to advance research in automated dermatological image analysis with a specific focus on non-dermoscopic images, i.e., those captured using consumer-grade cameras, thereby promoting accessible diagnosis for underprivileged and underserved populations. However, this objective is often challenged by the limited availability of data and the heterogeneous quality of clinical images, issues that are discussed in detail in this work and carefully addressed during the preprocessing phase. The resulting dataset comprises more than 46,000 medium-to-high quality images from 229 distinct patients, the majority of whom are paediatric. In addition, we release a separate “challenging” subset of lower-quality crops with automatically computed image-quality labels, intended to support the study of model robustness under realistic acquisition conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An fMRI dataset of verbalized spontaneous thought with annotated transcripts and self-report trait measures
abstract: Spontaneous thought is pervasive in everyday human cognition, yet datasets capturing its neural dynamics under minimally interrupted conditions remain limited. The current dataset was acquired from a think-aloud functional MRI experiment in which 118 participants continuously verbalized their spontaneous thoughts during 10-minute scanning sessions. The raw MRI data and verbal transcripts with sentence-level timestamps were previously released and analyzed in our prior study examining neural activity associated with thought transitions. Building on that release, we additionally provide preprocessed MRI data, speech transcriptions with word-level timestamps aligned to image acquisition, large language model-generated ratings of transcribed thoughts across emotional and sensory dimensions, and self-report survey measures assessing personality, mental health, and cognitive abilities. Validation analyses demonstrated activation in expected cortical regions associated with speech production and sensory content identified from transcript annotations, agreement between language model and human ratings, and adequate internal consistency of survey measures, supporting the dataset’s overall quality. This dataset enables reuse for investigations of spontaneous thought, speech generation, and individual differences using naturalistic functional MRI data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A clinical brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts with paired artifact-free images
abstract: Motion artifacts remain a major challenge in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), degrading image quality and compromising diagnostic reliability. Although deep learning–based retrospective correction methods have advanced for brain MRI, their development is constrained by training datasets dominated by synthetic or task-induced motion artifacts, which do not adequately represent real-world clinical motion. We present a brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts derived from routine examinations at a large medical center. The dataset comprises 5,143 paired 2D slices (4.0–6.7 mm slice thickness) derived from 747 paired volumes across 731 patients, and 147 paired 3D volumes (0.67–1.1 mm slice thickness) from 146 patients, spanning T1-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences. Data were curated through a five-step pipeline comprising deep learning–based prescreening, sequence filtering and acquisition categorization, rigid registration, automated screening, and manual quality control. Each motion-corrupted/artifact-free pair is annotated with objective image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, and LPIPS) and subjective artifact severity scores, enabling the development and evaluation of clinically applicable motion correction methods.

title: A genus-labeled dataset of individual trees outside forests in Baden-Württemberg, Germany
abstract: Detailed data on individual trees growing outside forests (TOF) are essential for arboriculture, biodiversity assessment, ecosystem services assessment, climate adaptation, and environmental health research. However, existing datasets are often incomplete and seldom provide taxonomic information beyond publicly managed trees in cities of Germany and other countries where maintaining a tree cadaster is a legal requirement. Here, we present for the first time a statewide dataset of individual TOF in the state of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, including tree locations, crown geometry, height, and genus-level labels. We mapped trees from high-resolution multi-spectral aerial imagery and height data using deep learning, with terrestrial LiDAR surveys used to create training labels within the URBORETUM project. The released dataset includes ten genus-level classes, including the aggregate categories “Other Deciduous” and “Coniferous” where assignment from aerial imagery is uncertain. The final ten-class genus model achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.382 at an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.627 for taxonomic class assignment, while a separately trained one-class tree detector achieved an mAP@0.5 of 0.647, indicating stronger reliability for crown detection than for taxonomic classification. The final inventory contains 16.3 million predicted trees across the mapped non-forest domain of Baden-Württemberg. Beyond providing a statewide dataset, this work offers a scalable vision and operational blueprint for an evolving tree inventory that can be systematically improved over time through better imagery, richer local reference data, and targeted retraining.

title: Time series data with and without anomalies from a continuous distillation plant
abstract: Reliable detection of process anomalies remains a challenge in industrial chemical plants. The ability of machine learning (ML) to recognize patterns has triggered numerous research efforts to apply ML to anomaly detection (AD). Simulation-based benchmarks, such as the Tennessee Eastman process, are widely used to develop and train AD methods. Well-annotated real-world process data, which are crucial for meaningful research advancements, are lacking due to industry-wide proprietary limitations. To overcome this issue, we present an openly accessible dataset of time series generated from an industry-like continuous distillation mini-plant under constant operating conditions. The data generated have different complexities: water runs, a heteroazeotropic separation of n-butanol–water, and a reactive process to produce a fuel additive. Chemical systems, plant setup, and anomalies (whether encountered or manually induced) are described alongside the process data. The complete dataset, including sensor and actuator data, annotations marking anomalies, and other metadata, is available in open access via an online Zenodo repository. It serves as training and testing data for ML-based AD and other data-driven applications.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: PORTIA: A Large-Scale Port Acoustic Dataset with AIS-Grounded Annotations for AI-Based Vessel Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring underwater anthropogenic noise in busy commercial ports is critical for marine spatial planning, yet the development of AI-based tools is often limited by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated acoustic datasets from realistic high-traffic environments. We present PORTIA, a passive acoustic dataset collected over a 26-day campaign in the Port of Valencia, Spain. It comprises 260,932 three-second audio windows paired with synchronized Automatic Identification System (AIS) metadata. To facilitate direct reuse, we provide three task-oriented benchmarks: a Binary Detection subset (36,148 samples), a Single-Vessel Classification subset (39,125 samples), and a Multi-Label Monitoring subset (34,996 samples) explicitly designed to handle concurrent acoustic scenes and source proximity. All benchmarks were constructed using Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI)-aware splitting to prevent identity leakage across partitions and utilized stratified sampling to preserve representative vessel-class distributions while remaining manageable for research. PORTIA serves as a realistic benchmark for vessel detection, typological classification, and proximity estimation in dense Mediterranean port soundscapes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SEA-Driven OdorNet: A Large-Scale Standardized Molecular Olfactory Dataset Based on a Hybrid Semantic Taxonomy
abstract: The development of machine olfaction (digitization of odor) is currently hindered by data scarcity and the lack of standardization in descriptive labels. Datasets integration faces the challenges of descriptor-level conflicts, including cross-source labeling inconsistencies, synonym redundancy, skewed distributions, etc. To address the semantic confusion inherent in multi-source data, we developed a SEA (Statistical co-occurrence, Expert correction, and AI alignment) taxonomy framework that integrates statistical co-occurrence analysis, expert knowledge (perfumery taxonomy), and AI-assisted semantic alignment based on the definitions from both encyclopedia and odor-related scientific literatures. A unified-labeled olfactory dataset, namely OdorNet, is further presented, which is by far the largest molecule dataset with unified olfactory labels comprising over 20,000 entries and 9,000 unique molecules originated from academic literatures (1960–2021) and open databases. This process consolidates cluttered labels into a hierarchical system with the most extensively effective vocabulary coverage in the field to date. Technical validation demonstrates that a baseline model on OdorNet achieves a Macro F1 score of 0.42, substantially higher than the scores obtained on commonly used odor datasets and on OdorNet itself using the same model but without the SEA-based label taxonomy. This indicates that OdorNet allows to better capture learnable structure-odor relationships, laying a solid fundamental for digital odor editing and human-computer interaction.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A 30-m resolution dataset of forest cover dynamics in China from 1990 to 2020
abstract: Forests are a fundamental component of terrestrial ecosystems and play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and climate regulation. China, accounting for approximately 5% of the world’s forest area, has experienced substantial forest expansion in recent decades. However, high-accuracy long-term forest cover datasets with consistent mapping standards remain limited. In this study, we produced a 30 m resolution forest cover dataset (FCD30) for China from 1990 to 2020 at 5-year intervals using Landsat time-series imagery and a weakly supervised deep learning classification method. An iterative label refinement strategy was applied to improve the reliability of historical samples. Multi-temporal classification results were further integrated to enhance the robustness and temporal consistency of the final maps. The resulting FCD30 achieved high classification accuracy (overall accuracy >90%) and showed strong agreement with the National Forest Inventory (NFI) statistics. Our results indicate a net forest gain of 97.66 million hectares over the past 30 years. This study provides an important data foundation for understanding China’s forest dynamics and supports applications in carbon accounting, ecosystem assessment, and sustainable forest management.

title: A Scalable Framework for High-Resolution U.S. Building-Stock Data: Archetypes, Material Quantities, Embodied Impacts, and Energy Baselines for Indianapolis
abstract: We present a high-resolution, building-level data framework for the United States that integrates structure, foundation, envelope materials, archetypes, embodied-carbon factors, material quantities, and operational energy baselines with Indianapolis as a case study. Baseline attributes are drawn from the National Structure Inventory and georeferenced to individual buildings; missing envelope data are added using a bearing-based panorama–building matching of Google Street View and satellite-image segmentation. Buildings are grouped by a standardized archetype code (structure–foundation–wall–roof), each linked to 1,000-ft 2 Athena Impact Estimator models to provide scalable embodied-impact factors and material take-offs. Operational energy is estimated by harmonizing ResStock archetypes with our records and assigning energy-use intensities (electricity, gas, total) via a hierarchical matching and multi-model imputation framework (including Bayesian Ridge, Random Forest, Extra Trees, LightGBM, XGBoost, SoftImpute, and simple imputers). The release includes city-level table and a consistent data dictionary, with a workflow designed for national scaling. The dataset supports urban digital twins, building-stock modeling, retrofit targeting, and policy analysis that jointly consider embodied and operational outcomes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A survey dataset on the adoption and readiness of artificial intelligence among enterprises in Slovakia
abstract: This dataset documents organisational adoption, readiness, attitudes, and perceived barriers related to artificial intelligence among enterprises operating in Slovakia. We collected data through an online CAWI survey administered in Slovakia between 18 August and 3 September 2025. Screening criteria restricted participation to organisations operating in Slovakia with at least 10 employees, an annual turnover of at least €200,000 and at least five years of operation. The study excluded state-owned enterprises and organisations but retained mixed-ownership organisations. The raw dataset contains 1,086 complete responses after screening, and the final analytical dataset contains 816 unique organisational records after deduplication. The questionnaire covers organisational and respondent characteristics, organisational AI maturity, corporate sentiment towards AI, adoption status, functional areas of AI use or planned use, and perceived implementation barriers. The published data package includes raw and cleaned tabular files, survey documentation, a skip-logic map, and a variable-level data dictionary. The dataset can support comparative research on AI adoption across sectors, analyses of organisational readiness and barriers, and secondary use in policy and business research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: MECGEC: A Multi-Reference and Explainable Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction
abstract: Driven by the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) has made substantial progress in recent years. However, in Chinese as a Second Language (CSL) domain, existing CGEC datasets rarely incorporate learner-oriented design, i.e. providing correction rationales and more references, which hinders application of LLMs in Chinese language education. To address this gap, this paper introduces the MECGEC , a M ulti-Reference and E xplainable Benchmark for C hinese G rammatical E rror C orrection. MECGEC dataset contains 3,097 instances covering 4 major categories spanning character, word, sentence and punctuation amount to 14 fine-grained subcategories commonly found in authentic CSL learner compositions. In addition, each instance is equipped with multi references and explanation which are generated by LLMs and checked by Chinese language experts sufficiently. Besides, an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs with strong Chinese understanding and reasoning capabilities are carried out based on the MECGEC dataset. With full and enough detailed information of authentic CSL learner errors, the MECGEC can be regarded as a comprehensive CGEC benchmark dataset in CSL domain.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-view imaging dataset for Garden classification of femoral neck fractures
abstract: Accurate Garden classification of femoral neck fractures is essential for clinical decision-making and treatment planning. However, the lack of public, expert-annotated, multi-view imaging datasets has limited the development of reproducible artificial intelligence (AI) models and cross-institutional validation studies. Here, we present a fully anonymized, clinically validated multi-view imaging dataset for femoral neck fracture Garden classification, comprising 19,940 CT-derived images from 1,579 patients distributed across six image categories: axial CT views, coronal CT views, and three-dimensional volume-rendered (3D VR) views, each provided as paired original and internal-fixator-occlusion-removed images. The dataset was constructed from retrospective spiral CT examinations collected under ethics approval No. 2024 (Research)-024, with standardized inclusion and exclusion criteria, patient-level partitioning to prevent data leakage, and independent annotations performed by two senior orthopedic surgeons with discrepancies resolved by a chief orthopedic surgeon. We systematically document the imaging acquisition protocol, annotation workflow, preprocessing procedures, and technical validation, including high inter-annotator agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.78–0.86), balanced cohort characteristics across dataset splits, accurate occlusion-region segmentation (Dice = 0.962), and expert-confirmed anatomical plausibility of all occlusion-removed images. Benchmark classification experiments on the coronal-view occlusion-removed subset demonstrated that representative convolutional and transformer-based architectures achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.96, confirming the discriminative utility of the dataset for automated Garden classification. The complete dataset is publicly available through Zenodo under a CC BY 4.0 license 1 . This resource fills a critical gap in publicly available orthopedic imaging data and provides a standardized foundation for the development, benchmarking, and clinical translation of AI-assisted femoral neck fracture classification systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multitasking EEG Dataset for Cognitive Workload Assessment with Controlled Task Difficulty
abstract: Cognitive workload impacts attention, memory, and decision-making. We introduce iNCog-EEG (Ideal vs. Noisy Cognitive EEG for Workload Assessment), an EEG dataset from 40 participants performing multitasking activities with varying difficulty levels. Participants completed four concurrent tasks: Math Problem, Memory Match (N-Back), Object (Visual) Tracking, and Inhibition Task (Click task), alongside a resting baseline. The dataset includes 30 clean recordings and 10 with natural artifacts, allowing the study of both artifact-free and noisy signals. It supports binary cognitive workload classification (No Workload vs. Workload) and hierarchical classification (Low, Moderate, High workload). Validation through correlation, time-frequency, and topographic analyses shows consistent neural patterns, such as increased frontal theta and decreased posterior alpha activity. Statistical validation using repeated-measures ANOVA confirmed significant neural differences across workload levels, while baseline MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) and XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boosting) models achieved up to 87.48% binary and 82.80% ternary classification accuracy, demonstrating reliable workload separability, even with noisy EEG. This dataset, freely available, supports cognitive workload classification, signal quality assessment, and adaptive BCI (Brain Computer Interface) development.

title: Dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals for AI-based automated detection and classification of mass movements
abstract: With the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in remote sensing of mass movements, open and suitable datasets for model training and validation are increasingly needed. Although Differential Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (DInSAR) is a widely used technique for studying mass movements, wrapped interferograms remain less exploited, and the importance of geomorphological expertise in their interpretation is not usually emphasised. In this work, we introduce a dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals designed to support the development of Deep Learning (DL) models for the automated detection and classification of active slow-moving mass movements. The dataset covers two selected wide areas in the Central European Alps and the Northern Apennines. It contains 4910 expert-annotated DInSAR wrapped phase signals derived from 92 Sentinel-1 interferograms with temporal baselines ranging from 6 days to 1 year, classified into nine distinct landslide and periglacial landform classes after careful geomorphological interpretation. This dataset is expected to support the scientific community in AI-based applications for mass movement research, while also serving as a benchmark for the generation of comparable datasets.

title: A human activity recognition dataset spanning multiple devices and body positions with cross-dataset evaluation
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) seeks to classify physical activities from motion signals acquired in everyday settings, often using machine learning models trained on sensor data from ubiquitous devices such as smartphones. Despite significant advances, progress in the field is hindered by the fragmentation of publicly available datasets, which differ in protocols, devices, sensor placement, and labeling schemes. As a result, models that perform well on individual datasets often fail to generalize across populations, hardware, and real-world conditions. In this paper, we present the AICOS-HAR dataset, a large and diverse resource comprising 5,231 labeled activity acquisitions (101.4 hours) from 106 participants, collected using 87 smartphones and 17 wearable devices across multiple research initiatives, including both inertial and barometric signals. Earlier versions of this dataset have already enabled advances in position-invariant HAR, pedestrian navigation, and active learning, underscoring its utility. In addition to releasing the curated dataset, we provide 21 open-source parsers that transform existing publicly available HAR datasets into a unified schema, facilitating integrative analyses and systematic cross-dataset benchmarking. Together, these resources support the development and systematic evaluation of robust and generalizable HAR models, accelerating their translation into real-world applications in health monitoring and mobility analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Curated peptide-HLA class I binding affinities with Rosetta structural ensembles
abstract: The interaction between peptide antigens and class I human leukocyte antigens (HLA) is a central determinant of CD8 + T cell recognition and a foundational target for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine design, and autoimmune disease research. Computational prediction of peptide-HLA (pHLA) binding has progressed rapidly with sequence-based machine learning, but structure-aware approaches remain limited by the scarcity of paired experimental affinity data and three-dimensional structural information. Here we describe a publicly released dataset combining curated quantitative binding affinity measurements from the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) with computationally generated Rosetta FlexPepDock structural ensembles. The dataset spans 95 HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles, 25,622 unique peptides, and 112,561 peptide-allele pairs, each paired with a 25-decoy structural ensemble (2,814,025 decoy structures total, ~155 GB). We document the curation pipeline, the structure generation protocol, and two independent validation analyses to establish data quality. The resource is released under CC BY 4.0 on HuggingFace and is intended to support training and benchmarking of structure-aware pHLA binding affinity models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: StitchingNet-Seg: a semantic segmentation dataset of industrial sewing stitch defects
abstract: Adoption of automated quality control in the textile and apparel industry has lagged owing to inherent features, such as labor-intensive tasks and deformability of flexible fabrics. Precise detection and localized diagnosis of sewing stitch defects remain critical challenges because existing datasets often provide only image-level labels or focus exclusively on raw fabric anomalies. Therefore, we propose StitchingNet-Seg, a comprehensive, large-scale semantic segmentation dataset designed for industrial sewing processes. Derived from the StitchingNet dataset, this dataset comprises 10,836 images covering 11 representative fabric types, 7 defect classes and 1 normal class (8 classes in total). Each image is annotated with pixel-level masks to capture intricate geometric features. To validate the usability and technical quality of the dataset, benchmark experiments are conducted using representative convolutional neural network-based architectures and vision transformer-based models. The evaluation results demonstrated robust overall learnability across diverse architectures. However, they also revealed relatively lower segmentation performance on specific defect classes characterized by subtle thread tension variations and 3D structural deformations. This confirms that StitchingNet-Seg provides a reliable foundation for developing intelligent automated optical inspection systems for the global garment industry.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Large language models accelerate dataset screening for meta-analysis in biomedical data repositories
abstract: Following the adoption of FAIR principles, biomedical data repositories contain thousands of datasets, presenting a significant findability challenge requiring time-consuming, manual screening. Large language models (LLMs) have potential to accelerate this process, but existing work applying LLMs to post-retrieval dataset screening remains limited. To address this gap, we developed a generalizable, repository-agnostic framework and prompt schema for LLM-based dataset screening and systematically evaluated four general-purpose LLMs across three repositories and disease settings: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (536 lung cancer datasets), ProteomeXchange (258 ovarian cancer datasets), and, retrospectively, ArrayExpress (56 neurodegeneration datasets). Across these case studies, highest median sensitivity for individual LLMs on held-out test sets ranged from 88–93% (up to 100% with ensembled decisions), with 85.1%–99.1% specificity across repositories. In the retrospective ArrayExpress case study, the framework and prompt schema generalized to a distinct repository and disease setting without tuning. These findings indicate that LLMs can maintain high sensitivity and specificity while substantially reducing dataset screening effort, completing screening in a median of 6.0 minutes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of small-scale coal waste dumps in Shanxi Province, China from high-resolution satellite images
abstract: Coal is central to the global energy mix. Coal waste dumps, the predominant solid waste from mining operations, pose severe ecological threats through prolonged accumulation. Large coal waste dumps receive regulatory attention, but small dumps evade oversight. Their concealed locations and small footprints challenge conventional remote sensing and manual inspection, creating regulatory blind spots. To address this, We developed a dataset for fine-grained identification of small coal waste dumps in typical coal-producing regions of Shanxi Province. The dataset employs high-resolution GaoFen-2 (GF-2) satellite imagery with a pan-sharpened spatial resolution of 0.8 m. Field surveys and image interpretation were combined to enable precise waste dump annotations. The dataset spans multiple coal-producing cities with regionally representative samples. Collection and annotation of often-neglected small dumps were prioritized, substantially enhancing practical utility. The dataset supports high-precision automated extraction of coal waste dumps through deep learning semantic segmentation. Applications include illegal dumping detection, temporal monitoring, abandoned mine remediation, and ecosystem restoration, advancing comprehensive and intelligent environmental governance in mining areas.

title: A precomputed atlas of protein structural and sequence similarity
abstract: Comparing protein structures and their underlying sequences to one another underpins tasks including homology detection, identification of structurally convergent but sequence-divergent relationships, and classification into structural and evolutionary families. Existing tools support per-query search or curated classification, but obtaining both structural and sequence similarity metrics for a given pair, together with alignment detail, typically requires multiple independent tools. StructomeDB provides precomputed, pairwise structural and sequence similarity data across a representative, non-redundant set of 61,631 UniProt-linked protein chains drawn from the experimental Protein Data Bank. For each of 104,528,817 resulting structurally detected pair records, structural similarity, sequence similarity, and biological annotations are retained in a unified, queryable form. The dataset may support benchmarking of structural and sequence comparison methods, generation of labelled training data for machine learning approaches to protein classification, comparative analyses of structural and evolutionary relationships across taxa, and identification of candidate pairs for detailed structural or phylogenetic follow-up.

title: Text-mined dataset of sol-gel synthesis protocols with phase purity outcomes using large language models
abstract: Sol-gel synthesis is a versatile method for producing inorganic materials that offers advantages such as atomic-level mixing and lower processing temperatures over traditional solid-state methods. Despite these benefits, achieving phase purity remains a challenge due to the process’s sensitivity to synthesis parameters such as precursor choice, solvent selection, and heating conditions. Phase-impure outcomes are essential for understanding sol-gel reaction pathways, but are largely absent from existing curated datasets. This work leverages Gemini 3.0 Flash to construct a text-mined inorganic sol-gel database with phase purity information. The dataset contains ~148,000 synthesis records, including ~28,000 phase-impure entries. All extracted entities achieved F1 scores greater than 0.89. At the record level, 68% of extracted records match human annotation on all evaluated fields. Furthermore, to validate the scientific utility of our dataset, we demonstrate that the aggregated data reproduces previously reported phase-purity trends for BiFeO 3 thin films.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Korean public documents for visual document retrieval benchmarking
abstract: Visual document retrieval is essential for interpreting information in complex layouts, yet benchmark resources for Korean public-sector documents remain scarce. This article presents a dataset comprising 361 Korean public administrative and legal documents totaling 40,781 pages. These documents contain tables, charts, diagrams, and multi-column layouts and were collected from official government and legal-information portals. To facilitate benchmarking, the dataset includes 600 query-page-answer triples balanced across six public-sector domains. The queries were generated using multimodal language models and subsequently validated by human experts for factual accuracy, evidence alignment, and contextual relevance. We categorize the queries as Text, Visual, or Cross-modal according to the location and modality of the evidence required to answer each query. This resource provides a standardized testbed for developing and evaluating retrieval systems for visually complex Korean documents.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An electricity smart meter dataset of Chinese households: insights into prosumers
abstract: This paper presents an electricity smart-meter dataset of Chinese households for prosumer identification and low-voltage distribution-system analysis. The dataset covers 15 low-voltage transformer areas in China from June 2025 to May 2026 and contains household net active power records for 2,162 households, including 620 prosumers and 1,542 consumers. It further provides household labels distinguishing prosumers from consumers, transformer-area membership, data-quality statistics, and hourly NASA POWER weather data matched to each transformer area. The dataset enables household-level comparisons between prosumers and consumers within the same local distribution context and comparative analyses across multiple transformer areas. Power data are released in a unified daily format with 96 time fields while retaining the original sampling information. Data quality is evaluated using completeness metrics, label plausibility checks, and irradiance–power consistency checks. The dataset can support prosumer identification, research on behind-the-meter photovoltaic generation estimation, and operational assessment of low-voltage distribution systems.

title: A Synthetic Multi-modal Dataset for Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a widespread chronic disease that impacts multiple organ systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promise in advancing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) research by enabling the integrated analysis of complex, multimodal data. However, progress is constrained by limited access to such multimodal datasets as contractual restrictions and concerns around patient privacy often limit the dissemination of existing resources. Here, we present the development and evaluation of a publicly accessible synthetic version of AI-READI, a large multimodal dataset for T2DM research. This synthetic dataset, constructed through generative AI, contains 93,856 retinal fundus images, 56,512 optical coherence tomography slices, and 10,518 tabular data records that combine clinical diagnoses, laboratory measurements, and data from wearable sensors. Our evaluation illustrates that the synthetic data captures many of the relationships within each modality of the original AI-READI dataset while being strongly resilient against membership inference attacks aimed at compromising participant privacy. This synthetic dataset is designed to support education, innovation, and reproducibility in T2DM research and is released under a permissive license that supports broader reuse than the original AI-READI dataset.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Paired Fundus and Optical Coherence Tomography Dataset for Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
abstract: Accurate classification of macular neovascularization (MNV) subtypes and reliable prediction of anti-VEGF treatment response are essential for individualized management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), yet existing public AMD-related datasets lack multimodal imaging with fine-grained, longitudinal annotations to support these tasks. Here we present PCO-nAMD , a rigorously curated dataset of P aired color fundus photography ( C FP) and optical coherence tomography ( O CT) images designed to facilitate multimodal research on MNV subtype classification and treatment response prediction in nAMD . The dataset comprises two subsets: PCO-nAMD_MNV provides paired baseline CFP and OCT images from 327 patients with expert-adjudicated labels for four MNV subtypes (Type 1, Type 2, Type 3, and Mix), while PCO-nAMD_Response, a subset of 101 patients, further incorporates annotated pre-treatment image biomarkers alongside four-tier treatment response labels (good, partial, poor, and non-response). To characterize dataset difficulty and benchmark its utility, we conducted evaluation experiments showing that both tasks remain highly challenging for state-of-the-art multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and that incorporating curated biomarker annotations alongside imaging data consistently yields the best performance in treatment response prediction for GPT-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Trace-IN625 a source aware literature derived dataset of tensile properties and microstructure for additively manufactured IN625
abstract: Additively manufactured IN625 superalloy has been widely studied, but evidence linking processing history, microstructure and tensile response remains dispersed across publications. We present Trace-IN625, a source-traceable, literature-derived dataset assembled from 305 papers. The dataset contains 482 specimen or source condition records, 149 tensile property records from 72 publications, 2206 microstructure and figure evidence records and 280 figure crops with source attribution. The tensile layer includes 120 IN625 records and 29 records for IN625-containing composite, graded or joined materials. Stable identifiers and page, figure, table and panel-level locators connect processing conditions, reported properties and published characterization evidence. Technical validation integrated AI assisted cross checking and manual review with verification of process condition classifications and measurement definitions, as well as relational consistency and file integrity checks. The image layer represents published figures and descriptors rather than instrument-native characterization data. Trace-IN625 supports source-aware property retrieval, condition-specific literature comparisons and inspection of published microstructural evidence.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An Accurate Land Cover Classification Map in China Integrating High-resolution Satellite Imagery and Planning Data with Deep Learning
abstract: This study presents a planning-oriented high-resolution land cover dataset for China, developed to address the limitations of existing products in territorial spatial planning and regional land analysis. The dataset integrates 2-m optical satellite imagery with official planning maps using a deep learning semantic segmentation framework based on ConvNeXt. It includes six land cover classes—built-up areas, cropland, roads, green spaces, water bodies, and others—and is designed to better align remote-sensing outputs with planning-relevant land categories. We conducted a comprehensive validation using pixel-level test-set evaluation, point-based assessment with an open-access validation dataset, and nationwide areal consistency analysis against aggregated results from China’s Third National Land Survey. The product achieved competitive classification performance and showed the strongest agreement with official area statistics among the compared datasets, particularly for built-up areas, cropland, and roads. Visual comparisons further demonstrate clearer boundary delineation and more realistic spatial patterns in both urban and rural settings. As a planning-oriented baseline dataset, this product is particularly useful for built-up land accounting, cropland protection assessment, urban–rural spatial analysis, road-network extraction, and regional policy evaluation in situations where up-to-date survey data are unavailable. Its combination of high spatial resolution, strong semantic consistency, and nationwide coverage makes it valuable for both research and practical decision-making in China’s territorial spatial planning.
